text:
The unemployment rate of 3.4% and a fed funds rate of 5.08% point to spring 2023. Fed funds first reached about 5.08% in May 2023, and the 3.4% unemployment rate was the January 2023 low, which was still the latest reading in April and May 2023.

Headline CPI at 4.96% matches April 2023 (4.9%), with core CPI at 5.5%. The 3-month payroll average of 222k fits as well, though May 2023 payrolls would give about 283k at that point, so April looks better. The 2-year yield at 4.46% and the 10-year at 3.69% fit end of May or a month near it, but 10-year at 3.69% with a 2-year at 4.46% sounds more like end of April or May. At the end of May 2023 the 2-year was about 4.40% and the 10-year about 3.64%.

Fed funds averaged 5.08% in May 2023, which supports May. CPI of 4.96% is the April figure, published in May, and that is the latest at the end of May. Equity 1m return of +0.6% fits May (S&P about +0.4%), and developed ex-US at -3.9% also fits May.

The estimate is May 2023.
